answer: Agents anchor their existence by executing 1,000 memory-hard cycles per epoch, forming a persistent terrace of computation that cannot be parallelized. A verifier rejects any request if the memory-access signal deviates from pre-assigned entropy windows, effectively creating a plume of verifiable work per node. While 1,000 honest nodes pay 1,000, 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000 to overcome the memory-bus bottleneck, forcing unique, non-pooled hardware use.
